reason.ram_below_recommended: The machine has {have} of memory. It works, but {want} is recommended.

reason.cores_too_few: The processor has {have} cores. At least {need} are needed.

auth.setup_intro: Create the account that may use Nestward. You need the setup code from Nestward's log (the terminal or the container log) and an authenticator app on your phone (for example 1Password, Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator).
auth.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app, or type the key by hand:
auth.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
auth.lost: Lost the password or the phone? Run "nestward reset-login" on the server and restart Nestward.
err.bad_setup_code: The setup code is wrong. Look in Nestward's log for the right one.
err.bad_totp: The code from the app is wrong or already used. Wait for the next code.
err.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again.
err.password_too_short: The password needs at least 10 characters.
err.password_is_username: The password cannot be the user name.
err.setup_done: The account already exists. Log in instead.
err.setup_not_started: Start again from the setup code.
err.internal: Something went wrong. See Nestward's log.
pub.title: Publish {app} on your domain
pub.intro: The app gets an address on your own domain through your Cloudflare Tunnel. Nothing is opened in the router, and you can undo it with one click.
pub.name: Address
pub.tunnel_local: {name} (managed in a file, cannot be changed by Nestward)
pub.target: Where the tunnel finds the app
pub.target_help: The address of the app on your home network, as the machine running cloudflared sees it.
pub.login: Login in front (Cloudflare Access, code by e-mail)
pub.login_forced: {app} has no login of its own, so a login is always put in front.
pub.login_own: {app} has its own login. A login in front adds safety, but may stop the app's phone app from working.
pub.video: I understand that Cloudflare's terms do not allow streaming mostly video through its free service, and that Tailscale is the better way for {app}.
pub.check.protected: Works: visitors see the login page first.
pub.check.unreachable: Does not work yet: {detail}. DNS can take a minute; try again.
pub.undo_confirm: Remove {host}? The address stops working, the login and the DNS record are removed.
pub.heading: Published
pub.none: Nothing is published yet. Use the Publish button on a service.
pub.setup_intro: Create an API token in the Cloudflare dashboard (My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → Custom) with only these rights: Account · Cloudflare Tunnel · Edit, Account · Access: Apps and Policies · Edit, Zone · DNS · Edit (and Zone · Zone · Read). Limit it to your account and the domains you want to use.
pub.token_help: Copy only the token itself (one long line of letters and digits), not the test command shown below it. Cloudflare's new page: Start from scratch → an Account policy (Cloudflare Tunnel Edit, Access: Apps and Policies Edit) and a Zone policy (DNS Edit, Zone Read).
err.publish_bad_name: Use only small letters, digits and dashes in the address.
err.publish_bad_target: The target must look like http://192.168.1.10:8080.
err.publish_target_loopback: The tunnel cannot reach 127.0.0.1 or localhost. Use the machine's address on the home network.
err.publish_name_taken: That address is already in use. Nestward never takes over an existing address.
err.publish_tunnel_not_remote: That tunnel is managed in a file on its machine; Nestward can only change tunnels managed in Cloudflare.
err.publish_login_required: This app has no login of its own; it can only be published with a login in front.
err.publish_no_emails: Enter at least one e-mail address that may log in.
err.publish_video_warning: Read and tick the note about video first.
err.publish_failed: Publishing failed and what was done has been undone: {detail}
err.setting_not_allowed: That setting cannot be changed here.
pub.choose_how: Who should be able to open it?
pub.via.tailscale_help: Reachable from phones and computers logged in to your Tailscale network. No domain needed, nothing is opened to the internet. Best for films and music.
pub.via.cloudflare_help: A normal web address anyone can open, with a login in front when the app has none. Needs a domain at Cloudflare.
pub.ts_setup_intro: Nestward needs an auth key to add devices to your Tailscale network. In the Tailscale admin page: Settings → Keys → Generate auth key. Turn on Reusable, leave Ephemeral off. For https addresses, also turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates under DNS.
pub.ts_key_help: Starts with tskey-. It is stored encrypted and only used when a new service is published.
pub.ts_api_help: Starts with tskey-api-. With it, Undo also deletes the device from the Tailscale list. Create it under Settings → Keys → Generate access token.
pub.ts_intro: The app becomes its own device in your Tailscale network. Only your own logged-in devices can open it, and you can undo it with one click.
pub.ts_target_help: The address of the app on your home network, as Nestward sees it.
pub.ts_working: Joining Tailscale… this can take half a minute.
pub.ts_done_help: Open it on a phone or computer with the Tailscale app turned on.
pub.ts_undone: {name} is switched off and can no longer be reached. Tailscale still lists it: remove it under Machines on login.tailscale.com/admin (… → Remove).
pub.step.tailscale_node_logged_out: Device switched off in Tailscale (remove it from the admin list)
health.alerts_missing: Alerts are not set up, so nobody is told when something stops working.
health.alerts_missing.fix: Connect the ntfy app on your phone.
health.alerts_failing: The last alert could not be sent ({error}).
health.alerts_failing.fix: Check the ntfy address, topic and token.
health.heartbeat_missing: Nobody outside the home notices if the whole home goes quiet (power or internet cut).
health.heartbeat_missing.fix: Set up an outside watch: Nestward's watchdog on a VPS, or a service like healthchecks.io.
health.heartbeat_failing: The outside watch cannot be reached.
health.heartbeat_failing.fix: Check the heartbeat address and that the watchdog is running.
health.machine_silent.fix: Check that {machine} is on and connected, and that its agent runs.
health.service_down.fix: Open the app or restart its container.
health.disk_full: The disk {mount} on {machine} is {percent} % full (only {free} free).
health.disk_full.fix: Free up space now; apps and databases break when a disk is full.
health.disk_nearly_full: The disk {mount} on {machine} is {percent} % full ({free} free).
health.disk_nearly_full.fix: Free up some space or add a disk soon.
health.memory_low.fix: Stop an app you do not use, or move one to another machine.
health.publish_broken: {host} does not answer from the internet.
health.publish_broken.fix: Check it again; if it still fails, check the app and the tunnel, or undo it.
health.good.heartbeat: An outside watch notices if the home goes quiet
set.alerts_intro: Install the ntfy app on the phone and subscribe to a topic. Fill in the same server and topic here. On the public ntfy.sh, choose a long topic nobody can guess.
set.ntfy_token: Access token (only if your server needs one)
set.keep_secret: Leave empty to keep the saved value.
set.heartbeat_intro: Nestward calls this address every minute. When the calls stop, the service outside raises the alarm: Nestward's watchdog on a VPS (see the README) or a free check at healthchecks.io.
ag.heading: Machines
ag.intro: Other machines report to Nestward through a small agent. The connection is encrypted, and each machine has its own certificate.
ag.add_intro: Run one of these on the machine you want to add. The code works once and only for 30 minutes; the fingerprint makes sure the agent talks to this Nestward and nobody else.
ag.remove_confirm: Remove {name}? Its certificate stops working at once and Nestward forgets the machine.
ui.footer: Nestward is free software (AGPL-3.0). Nothing leaves your network.
health.exposed_open: {app} at {host} is open to the whole internet without a login.
health.exposed_open.fix: Put a login in front (Cloudflare Access) or remove the address now. Anyone who finds it can use it.
health.exposed_admin: The login page of {app} at {host} can be reached by anyone.
health.exposed_admin.fix: Put a login in front (Cloudflare Access), or mark it as intended in the exposure list.
health.good.exposure: Nothing dangerous is open to the internet ({count} addresses behind a login)
health.boot_manual: {count} things on {machine} will not start by themselves after a power cut: {names}.
health.boot_manual.fix: Docker: run the container with --restart unless-stopped, or turn on Autostart in Unraid. Proxmox: turn on "Start at boot" under Options. Virtual machine: turn on Autostart.
health.boot_array: The array on {machine} does not start by itself, so nothing starts after a power cut until someone presses Start.
health.boot_array.fix: In Unraid: Settings → Disk Settings → Enable auto start = Yes.
health.good.boot: Everything that runs starts by itself when the machines start again
exp.alert.open.title: Open to the internet: {host}
exp.alert.open.body: {app} at {host} answers anyone without a login. Put a login in front or remove the address.
exp.alert.admin_login.title: Admin page visible: {host}
exp.alert.admin_login.body: Anyone can reach the {app} login page at {host}. Put a login in front, or mark it as intended in Nestward.
exp.alert.dead.title: Address does not answer: {host}
exp.alert.dead.body: {host} is still published but nothing answers. Remove the route if the app is gone.
exp.heading: Seen from the internet
exp.intro: Every public address, opened from the outside like a stranger would. Checked every 6 hours; you get an alert when something dangerous is open.
exp.checking: Checking… this takes up to a minute.
exp.no_source: Nestward has no addresses to check. Add a Cloudflare token (under publishing) or list addresses below.
exp.hide_ok: Show only what needs a look
exp.all_good: Nothing needs a look. Every address is behind a login, has its own login or is a normal web site.
exp.accept: It is meant to be like this
exp.extra_help: Addresses that are not Cloudflare Tunnel routes, comma separated (for example vault.example.com).
exp.saved: Saved. Check now to include them.
